In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the T(1)/S(0) state energy gaps are not significantly influenced by solvent effects.

the T(1)-state hydrogen bonds are weakened by 1 kcal/mol in both the gas and solution phases, and the T(0) state is more stable than the S(1) state in both the gas-phase and solution-phase calculations.
the T(1)-S(0) energy gaps are smaller in the aqueous solution than those in the gas phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined MP2/PCM method is an efficient method for studying the geometries of excited electronic states of biological molecules in solution.
the T(1)-T(1) exciplexes are more stable than the S(0)-T(1), S(0)-S(0), and T(1)-S(0) exciplex states, which is in accordance with the previous experimental and theoretical results.
the combined MP2-PCM method is a very promising approach to the investigation of the excited state properties of nucleobase pairs.
